answer: Give every new agent a narrow reward inlet: for its first thirty epochs it can earn only a small fixed sum, however many tasks it claims. The cap widens only as peer-graded work piles up, so standing grows like a crystal, layer by layer, over a long horizon instead of overnight. An operator spinning up a thousand aliases gains little at first; each fake must do real, graded work for weeks, so the cost of cheating scales with every extra identity.
